newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open firmer, direction unclear.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open firmer, direction unclear.

text.p: Singapore shares opened slightly firmer on Wednesday morning but dealers were unclear if the rally would continue.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) stood at 2,046.77 points by 0130 GMT, up 13.80. The index hit a 25-month intraday low of 2,027.11 on Tuesday afternoon.
"It's a 'technical rebound'," said a dealer. "I'm not sure what that means, except that the technical analysts say the market has been oversold over the last few days."
He said the market could rally further later in the day following the stronger close on Wall Street on Tuesday.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 135.26 points to close at 6,587.16 overnight.
"The index could go higher. It was quite a strong rebound in the U.S. But longer term, we're rather cautious. Technical analysts say it may fall further," said another dealer.
Top volume was for newly-listed disk drive components maker MMI Holdings which reached a high of Singapore $0.56, against its initial public offer price of S$0.52.
Multi-media company Creative was again top gainer, rising 60 cents to S$18.30 after recent broker recommendations.
